behavior: Highly social and vocal; usually forages in flocks on the ground or in shallow water, eating varied plant and animal foods. Large groups gather at communal roosts, while displaying males ruffle their plumage, fan the tail, and point the bill upward.
field_marks: Exceptionally long, tapered tail, often folded into a V-shaped keel
Adult male glossy blue-black to violet-black overall
Female dark brown above and warmer buff-brown below
Adult pale-yellow eye contrasts with the dark head
Stout, straight black bill and flat-headed profile
Long, dark legs and slender body
habitat: Open and semi-open landscapes, especially near water, including marsh edges, irrigated fields, farmland, lawns, parks, groves, and thickets; generally absent from dense forest and waterless desert.
